answer: Each identity claims one shale outcrop and locks a 70-credit nebula bond. It files each epoch a key-signed depth, dip angle, and nebula serial no second outcrop may reuse. An auditor recomputes the angle from the zephyr table; an error over 3 degrees, a reused serial, or a copied record burns the bond. First survey 38; the k-th fake pays 38+5(k-1), as deeper zones need longer traverses, so the 1000th pays 5033 and 1000 fakes cost 2,535,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-outcrop ring fails: one serial ties one key to one outcrop, and replay exposes mismatches. An honest surveyor pays 38 once.
